children: Shares of Global Payments (GPN) jumped 11% on Friday, clocking its best day since February, after reports that private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice is pursuing a take-private deal for it.

According to a report in The Financial Times, CD&R has teamed up with GTCR, Global Payments’ largest shareholder, on a joint bid for the payments processor. Talks remain ongoing, and a deal may not materialize, the report said, while adding that any transaction would likely include a premium to the recent trading price. Shares of Global Payments closed at $96.84 on Friday, giving the company a market valuation of $25.6 billion.
William Blair Estimates Deal At $101 Per Share

William Blair kept its 'Market Perform' rating after the report. The firm called the story “credible,” noting that GTCR owns roughly 15% of Global Payments. The company’s nearly $22 billion of net debt could complicate a leveraged buyout, especially if rates stay elevated, the firm said. Blair estimates a take-private could land near $101 per share and said anything higher “feels rich” compared with better-positioned fintech peers. The firm put the odds of a completed deal “comfortably below” 50%. If a transaction does occur, Blair expects greater pressure on other highly leveraged public fintechs such as Fiserv and Shift4 Payments to sell themselves.
B.Riley Sees A Range Of Possible Outcomes

In a private-equity scenario, B. Riley sees a wide range of possible outcomes, from a low of $84 to a high of $190. It continues to view Global Payments as “materially mispriced,” reiterated its 'Buy' rating, and highlighted its $194 price target as the highest on the Street.
